restaurant_name: CSDC Dental Clinic สาขา สันทราย
text:
I started my orthodontic consultations with Dr. Chanakan on November 16, 2022, one month after giving birth to my first child. The treatment is still ongoing, and while I've been attending regularly, I haven't completely stopped. There was a period when I had a photoshoot for a sportswear collection, but my orthodontic treatment prevented it. I consulted Dr. Chanakan about whether the treatment would be completed in time, and she said it should, but they would need to monitor for any loose wires or other damage. Ultimately, I missed the photoshoot because it wasn't finished on time. Then, about two months ago, the wires shifted, even though I was experiencing severe morning sickness with my second child and could barely eat. The shift caused a sore on my cheek, requiring three visits to have the wires removed. I admit that this year I've had many appointments postponed, but never more than two to three months apart. This was due to my first child being hospitalized and my second pregnancy (which I didn't realize I had, thinking it was an intestinal issue requiring weekly doctor visits). Another reason is that Dr. Chanakan is only available two days a month. I have to schedule appointments during her hours; if my child is hospitalized or I need to see her, I have to reschedule. (For those who are short on time, you should check with other doctors to see if they have more frequent appointments.) And most recently, just a few days ago... We asked the doctor how much longer it would be before we could have the braces removed. We asked because we're due in November and need to plan our schedule. We didn't intend to rush the doctor, but the response we got was that the doctor's schedule is inconsistent, making it difficult to assess the situation. (Our reason is that our child is frequently hospitalized, and we're also hospitalized ourselves.) We only asked for a rough estimate because the doctor is the one who really knows. There's no need to seem so annoyed by the question. Our schedules don't always align, especially with a child. You'll understand how difficult it is for a mother to go anywhere when something goes wrong. For anyone considering this clinic, if this doctor is convenient for you, that's great. But if not, consider a doctor who's more frequent, so you can go in the middle or end of the month if you can't make it. Everything else is fine; the staff and facilities are excellent.

P.S. For the appointments we missed or postponed, we have medical certificates proving that our child was hospitalized at the time and that we were also receiving treatment there. We didn't postpone to get criticized; it was absolutely necessary.
